headline: Nvidia predicts $108 billion quarterly revenue, driven by data centers
summary: The chip giant's data center revenue more than doubled year-over-year to a record $89 billion, fueling massive profit growth.
details: Nvidia has announced record-breaking financial results, reporting $96.2 billion in revenue for the past quarter. This represents a significant increase of over $10 billion from the previous quarter.

The company's data center business was the primary driver of this growth, with revenue more than doubling year-over-year to an astounding $89 billion. This surge highlights the immense demand for AI and high-performance computing infrastructure.
Overall profits for Nvidia also saw a substantial jump, more than doubling to $59.7 billion. This financial performance positions Nvidia as a major player in the global tech economy.

While the data center business soared, Nvidia's 'edge computing' category, which includes its consumer gaming segment, generated $7.2 billion. This segment saw a 27% year-over-year increase, though it was tempered by slower consumer PC sales and elevated component prices.

Looking ahead, Nvidia is forecasting an impressive $108 billion in revenue for the upcoming quarter. This projection places Nvidia among tech giants like Amazon, Apple, and Alphabet, which have also achieved over $100 billion in quarterly revenue.
caption:
Nvidia is on track to become a $100 billion-a-quarter company, with its data center business booming.

Nvidia has announced record-breaking financial results, reporting $96.2 billion in revenue for the past quarter. This represents a significant increase of over $10 billion from the previous quarter.

The company's data center business was the primary driver of this growth, with revenue more than doubling year-over-year to an astounding $89 billion. This surge highlights the immense demand for AI and high-performance computing infrastructure.

Overall profits for Nvidia also saw a substantial jump, more than doubling to $59.7 billion. This financial performance positions Nvidia as a major player in the global tech economy.

While the data center business soared, Nvidia's 'edge computing' category, which includes its consumer gaming segment, generated $7.2 billion. This segment saw a 27% year-over-year increase, though it was tempered by slower consumer PC sales and elevated component prices.

Looking ahead, Nvidia is forecasting an impressive $108 billion in revenue for the upcoming quarter. This projection places Nvidia among tech giants like Amazon, Apple, and Alphabet, which have also achieved over $100 billion in quarterly revenue.
